question.worked_solution:
First, we take the natural logarithm $(ln)$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{5}^{x+3} & ={2}^{5-4x} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({5}^{x+3}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({2}^{5-4x})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify both sides of the equation. This gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+3)\operatorname{ln}⁡(5) & =(5-4x)\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we solve for $x$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+3)\operatorname{ln}⁡(5) & =(5-4x)\operatorname{ln}⁡(2) \\ x\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)+3\operatorname{ln}⁡(5) & =5\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)-4x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2) \\ x\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)+4x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2) & =5\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)-3\operatorname{ln}⁡(5) \\ x(\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)+4\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)) & =5\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)-3\operatorname{ln}⁡(5) \\ x & =\frac{5\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)-3\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)+4\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)}\end{aligned}
$$
